title: Auto-incident staging and operator playbook insertions
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary:
Build an automated incident-staging service that prepares a contextual incident bundle and inserts curated operator playbook fragments into PagerDuty incidents and Slack incident threads. The goal is to reduce time-to-first-action for oncall engineers by surfacing the most relevant traces, a short impact estimate, suggested remediation steps (playbook snippets), and a pre-populated postmortem draft when an incident is acknowledged.

Why this work:
- PagerDuty and Slack alerts often lack the contextual artifacts needed for fast mitigation (relevant traces, slow query keys, affected routes).
- Manual runbook lookup and copying slows initial triage and increases mean time to acknowledge (MTTA) and mean time to resolution (MTTR).
- Creating a draft postmortem at the start of a major incident reduces friction and ensures timeline capture.

Scope and non-goals:
- Scope: PD webhook enrichment, Slack thread attachments, runbook fragment selection algorithm, lightweight postmortem draft creation, idempotent enrichment to avoid noisy duplicates, deduplication heuristics for repeated flapping alerts.
- Out of scope: full automatic remediation, deep root-cause automation, rewriting entire runbooks (we will insert fragments and links only).

Core components to deliver:
1) Incident-staging API (internal): given an alert payload, gather top-3 traces, top slow endpoints, recent related error logs, and produce a compact "incident bundle" JSON. 
2) Playbook fragment selector: heuristic + ML reranker that matches incident bundle signals to runbook snippets (with confidence score).
3) PagerDuty enrichment flow: add a concise summary, link to bundle, attach suggested playbook snippets and links to dashboards. Must adhere to PD rate limits and use PD API v2.
4) Slack incident thread composer: post ephemeral summary and expandable blocks with traces/sparkline latency, and a button to open the pre-populated postmortem draft in Confluence or Drive.
5) Postmortem draft generator: create a private stub document with initial timeline entries and estimated impact ranges based on tokenized request counts and error percentages.

Acceptance criteria (must all be true):
- When a high-severity (SEV > 1) PagerDuty incident is created, the system enriches the incident within 60s with a bundle that includes: 3-trace links, top-3 affected routes, and 2 suggested runbook fragments (strings and links).
- Slack enrichments appear in the incident channel thread without creating duplicate messages for the same incident within 10 minutes.
- Postmortem draft is created and linked only for incidents that transition to acknowledged AND have an estimated user impact > 0.5% of typical QPS.
- Enrichment attempts must be idempotent and retry on 429 from PD with exponential backoff.
- Security review checklist completed and SSO-limited service account used for Playbook editor links.

Tasks (implementation checklist):
- Design API contract for Incident-staging service and publish OpenAPI spec.  
- Implement trace/metrics/log selectors (kafka consumer + short TTL cache).  
- Implement playbook fragment store (read-only, versioned YAML snippets).  
- Integrate with PagerDuty v2 REST API for incident note creation and attachments.  
- Build Slack composer using Block Kit and verify formatting on mobile and web.  
- Implement postmortem draft creation using Confluence API; fallback to Drive when Confluence unavailable.  
- Add feature flags for PD enrichment and Slack compose.  
- Add telemetry: metrics for enrichment latency, pd_enrich_failures, duplicate_msgs_prevented, postmortem_created_count.  
- Add e2e tests (local PD mock + slack mock) and a small load test for 200 concurrent alerts/min.

Testing plan:
- Unit tests for playbook selection and dedupe logic.
- Integration tests against PD sandbox account; validate idempotency and 429 backoff.
- Manual QA in staging: trigger synthetic latency spike, then assert Slack and PD enrichment content and links open to real traces/dashboards.
- Canary rollout to 10% of teams (observability, runtime, core-api) and monitor enrichment error rate and PD rate-limit metrics.

Rollout plan:
- Week 1: API and playbook fragment store + tests (feature flag off).
- Week 2: PD enrichment integration + unit/integration tests (internal PD sandbox).
- Week 3: Slack composer, postmortem draft generator, telemetry + security review.
- Week 4: Canary with 3 teams, collect feedback and iterate.
- Week 5: Ramp to org with opt-out toggle per-svc.

Security & compliance notes:
- Service account for PD/Slack must use least privilege and be scoped to create notes and webhooks only; audit logs enabled.
- Any linkable trace data must not include PII; sanitize spans with parameterized values.
- Security review required before canary; add to security sprint for week 2.

Links and artifacts:
- Design sketch (drive): https://drive.redwood.ai/obs/incident-staging/sketch-v1
- OpenAPI draft: https://git.redwood.ai/obs/incident-staging/openapi.yaml
- Playbook fragment format spec: https://docs.redwood.ai/playbooks/fragments.md
- Confluence template: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Incident+Postmortem+Template
- Related PRs (TBD), PD sandbox creds in 1Password path: obs/incidents/pd-sandbox

Known risks & mitigations:
- Risk: PD rate limits may throttle enrichment bursts. Mitigation: central rate-limiter token bucket in service and exponential backoff.
- Risk: Playbook fragment mismatch yields low trust from oncall. Mitigation: include confidence score and a "suggestion reason" summary; allow manual feedback in Slack.
- Risk: Sensitive data leakage. Mitigation: sanitize traces and run security review early.

Metrics to watch after launch:
- PD_enrich_latency_p50/p95 (target p95 < 60s)
- pd_enrich_failure_rate (target < 1%)
- postmortem_draft_conversion_rate (how many drafts turned into full PMs)
- mean_time_to_ack (MTTA) for teams with enrichment enabled (expected >10% improvement)

Additional notes:
- We should add a small "feedback" button to Slack that appends operator feedback to the fragment store for future retraining iterations.
- Consider a future phase that auto-suggests an on-call owner based on recent deployers and service ownership metadata.
acceptance_criteria: PD incidents enriched within 60s with 3 traces, top-3 routes, 2 runbook fragments
Slack thread enrichment is deduplicated within 10 minutes
Postmortem draft created only for acknowledged incidents with >0.5% impact
Retries and exponential backoff on 429 from PD
Security review completed and service account scoped
comments: 2026-03-09 - Maya Chen: Created ticket to centralize enrichment flows for PD/Slack and reduce MTTR. Initial spike showed ~18% time saved in triage for a few internal incidents.

2026-03-11 - Priya Nair (SRE): Please ensure we include sampling controls so we don't attempt postmortem drafts for low-impact noise alerts. Also flagged data privacy review.
2026-03-12 - Samir O'Neill (Security): Security review kickoff scheduled. Need to document span scrub rules and service account IAM policy before canary.

decisions: Use PD API v2 for note creation and attachments to avoid legacy webhooks.
Playbook fragments stored as versioned YAML in git + read-only cache to avoid runtime editing complexity.
Confluence primary for postmortem drafts; fallback to Drive if Confluence API rate-limited or unavailable.
risks: PD rate limits causing delayed enrichments - mitigated by token-bucket rate limiter and backoff
Low-quality fragment suggestions reducing trust - mitigated by confidence and feedback loop
Sensitive span data leak - mitigated by span sanitization rules and security review
rollout_plan: Week 1: API + fragment store behind feature flags
Week 2: PD integration + integration tests in PD sandbox
Week 3: Slack composer + postmortem draft generator
testing_plan: Unit tests for selection and dedupe logic
Integration tests against PD sandbox and Slack staging
Manual QA with synthetic latency spike and error flood
Load test 200 alerts/min to validate rate limiter behavior
